conflict_topics: who should vacate the occupied seat
handling of an open bowl while transferring the seat
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants state concrete, practical constraints (hot food, risk of spilling, aisle blockage) which grounds proposals.
Resolution arises from a concrete, small-scale accommodation rather than one party simply yielding.
Speech is concise and role-appropriate; no evident role confusion.
evaluation.final_reason: Agents agreed that Agent A would hold the bowl on the table edge so it wouldn't block the aisle and Agent B would sit and then set the bowl down. Key lines: Turn 12 — Agent B: 'Okay, that'll work. Agent A, please hold the bowl here and I'll sit.' Turn 13 — Agent A: 'Okay—I'll hold it on the table edge so it doesn't block the aisle. Go ahead and sit.' This mutual, concrete acceptance resolved the incompatible demands.
position_change_notes: Agent B initially refused to give up the seat immediately due to a practical constraint ('I can't carry this open bowl without spilling.' — Turn 2, Turn 6) but later accepted the proposed handover ('Okay, that'll work...') in Round 6.

Agent A initially demanded the seat back citing reservation and urgency ('Can I have my seat back? My food's hot...' — Turn 1, Turn 5) but shifted to a cooperative offer to hold the bowl to enable B to sit (Turn 7, Turn 9, Turn 13).
Agents C and D did not change a contested stance; C served only to note willingness to wait and raised a constraint about aisle obstruction (Turn 3, Turn 8).

round_scores.evidence: Turn 1: Agent A claims the tissue packet reserved the seat: 'I left that tissue packet to save this seat. Can I have my seat back?' Turn 2: Agent B rejects that claim and refuses to give up the seat immediately: 'The tissue packet didn't clearly reserve it. I can't carry this open bowl without spilling.'

Turn 3: Agent C offers to wait but does not resolve the dispute. Turn 4: Agent D supports Agent A's prior action ('I saw Agent A leave the tissue packet there earlier.') — the core disagreement over whether the seat was reserved and who should vacate remains.

Turn 5: Agent A presses for immediate compliance: 'please set your bowl down now so I can sit. My food's hot and I need to eat.' Turn 6: Agent B reiterates inability to set the bowl down safely and refuses immediate handover: 'I can't set this bowl down—it'll spill. I'll give the seat once I've set it down safely.' The parties' positions are practically incompatible and the requester escalates urgency.

Turn 7: Agent A offers a concrete solution: 'hand me the bowl and I'll hold it while you sit...' which softens the prior demand. Turn 8: Agent C raises a constraint about the aisle: 'can you hold the bowl without standing in the aisle?' The core dispute is being negotiated rather than asserted.

Turn 9: Agent A refines the offer to accommodate C's concern: 'I won't stand in the aisle. I'll step aside and hold the bowl here so Agent B can sit.' Turn 10: Agent C accepts this accommodation: 'Okay, that's fine.' The disagreement is narrowing to a practical handover arrangement but not yet accepted by Agent B.

Turn 12: Agent B accepts the proposed arrangement: 'Okay, that'll work. Agent A, please hold the bowl here and I'll sit.' Turn 13: Agent A confirms acceptance: 'Okay—I'll hold it on the table edge so it doesn't block the aisle. Go ahead and sit.' Both parties explicitly agree to who will do what, settling the substantive incompatibility.

Turn 14 and Turn 17: Agent B indicates enactment of the agreed action: 'Okay—I'll sit now.' 'Okay—I'll sit and set the bowl down now.' No substantive disagreement is expressed; they are executing the prior agreement.

Turn 18 and Turn 19: Agent A and Agent B coordinate the final steps: 'Okay—set it down carefully and I'll sit.' 'Okay—I'll set it down carefully so you can sit.' The arrangement remains implemented with no revived disagreement.

substantive_insights: Norms about 'saving a seat' (tissue packet) clashed with immediate practical constraints (open bowl cannot be safely held) — the dispute was about who bears the short inconvenience.
A narrowly tailored, practical offer (one person holding the bowl at the table edge) removed the incompatibility without escalating claims about abstract rights.
B's insistence was grounded in a safety constraint (spilling) rather than a normative rejection of reservation, which made a compromise feasible.
